newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico outlines rules for Pacific-North railway.
newsitem.headline: Mexico outlines rules for Pacific-North railway.

text.p: Mexico's Transport Ministry outlined the rules that will govern bidding in the auction for the Pacific-North railway, the country's largest rail link.
The government will auction 80 percent ownership in the 6,520-km railway and grant a 50-year concession, according to a statement by the ministry.

It added the concession will also include a 25 percent stake in the Mexico City railway terminal and also the right to exploit the old Chihuahua-Pacific railway line that runs through the famed Copper Canyon.
Following conclusion of the deal, the government will have 81 months in which to offer the remaining 20 percent of the railway ownership on the Mexican Stock Exchange, the statement said.

The government will begin accepting proposals June 19 and begin accepting bids on June 26. It will award the concession on July 7, it said. It added that 45 percent of the country's cargo is currently moved on the railway's lines.
